explanation_en: This expression is used to describe an effort or action that produced no result or was useless. It is very common in both written and spoken Spanish, fitting well in B2/C1 contexts. A common pitfall is trying to translate 'in vain' literally using incorrect prepositions; 'en vano' is a fixed phrase.

examples.en_text: I studied all night for the exam, but it was in vain because they canceled it.
examples.target_text: Estudié toda la noche para el examen, pero fue en vano porque lo cancelaron.

examples.en_text: I tried to convince my brother not to buy that car, but it was in vain.
examples.target_text: Intenté convencer a mi hermano de que no comprara ese coche, pero fue en vano.

examples.en_text: We searched for the keys all over the house in vain; in the end, they were in the car.
examples.target_text: Buscamos las llaves por toda la casa en vano; al final estaban en el coche.

examples.en_text: I don't want you to think that all your effort has been in vain.
examples.target_text: No quiero que pienses que todo tu esfuerzo ha sido en vano.

examples.en_text: We prepared everything for the garden party, but it rained and the work was in vain.
examples.target_text: Preparamos todo para la fiesta en el jardín, pero llovió y el trabajo fue en vano.

examples.en_text: We waited in line for more than an hour in vain, as the tickets had already sold out.
examples.target_text: Esperamos más de una hora en la fila en vano, ya que las entradas se habían agotado.

explanation_en: 'Jugarse' means to risk or gamble, and 'sustento' refers to one's livelihood or means of support. Together, this collocation is highly idiomatic and used to describe high-stakes situations where basic survival or financial stability is put at risk. It carries a strong emotional weight and is common in journalistic or formal spoken registers.

examples.en_text: I can't just leave my office job like that; I don't want to risk my livelihood.
examples.target_text: No puedo dejar mi trabajo de oficina así como así; no quiero jugarme mi sustento.

examples.en_text: If you keep arguing with the boss like that, you are risking your livelihood.
examples.target_text: Si sigues discutiendo con el jefe de esa manera, te estás jugando tu sustento.

examples.en_text: They decided to invest all their savings in that company and ended up gambling away their livelihood.
examples.target_text: Ellos decidieron invertir todos sus ahorros en esa empresa y terminaron jugándose su sustento.

examples.en_text: We know that by going on strike we are risking our livelihood, but it is necessary.
examples.target_text: Sabemos que al hacer esta huelga nos estamos jugando nuestro sustento, pero es necesario.

examples.en_text: He decided to quit gambling because he realized he was risking his livelihood.
examples.target_text: Él decidió dejar el juego porque se dio cuenta de que se estaba jugando su sustento.

examples.en_text: Don't sign that contract without reading it carefully; you are risking your livelihood.
examples.target_text: No firmen ese contrato sin leerlo bien; se están jugando su sustento.

explanation_en: This figurative expression means to lose focus, lose control, or go astray while trying to achieve a goal. It is widely used in personal narratives, self-help contexts, and literature to describe moral or psychological derailment. Learners should note that it uses the pronominal form 'perderse' rather than the simple 'perder'.

examples.en_text: If we don't bring a map, it's very easy to get lost along the way.
examples.target_text: Si no llevamos un mapa, es muy fácil perderse en el camino.

examples.en_text: She didn't know the city and got lost on the way to my house.
examples.target_text: Ella no conocía la ciudad y se perdió en el camino a mi casa.

examples.en_text: We left early, but we got lost along the way because of the GPS.
examples.target_text: Salimos temprano, pero nos perdimos en el camino por culpa del GPS.

examples.en_text: Follow the road signs so that you don't get lost along the way.
examples.target_text: Sigue las señales de tráfico para que no te pierdas en el camino.

examples.en_text: I prefer to take a taxi because I'm afraid of getting lost along the way.
examples.target_text: Prefiero tomar un taxi porque temo perderme en el camino.

examples.en_text: The guests haven't arrived yet; they surely got lost along the way.
examples.target_text: Los invitados aún no han llegado; seguro se perdieron en el camino.

explanation_en: This figurative expression is used to describe a central focus or obsession in someone's life or a main topic of discussion. It is a sophisticated alternative to 'tratarse de' or 'centrarse en,' making it perfect for B2/C1 learners. It can be used with both physical objects and abstract concepts, maintaining a neutral to formal register.

examples.en_text: Today's meeting is going to revolve around the new budgets.
examples.target_text: La reunión de hoy va a girar en torno a los nuevos presupuestos.

examples.en_text: The whole movie revolves around an unsolved mystery.
examples.target_text: Toda la película gira en torno a un misterio sin resolver.

examples.en_text: Since her son was born, her life revolves around him.
examples.target_text: Desde que nació su hijo, su vida gira en torno a él.

examples.en_text: The political debate revolved around public education.
examples.target_text: El debate político giró en torno a la educación pública.

examples.en_text: Our marketing strategy must revolve around the customer's needs.
examples.target_text: Nuestra estrategia de marketing debe girar en torno a las necesidades del cliente.

examples.en_text: In our solar system, the planets revolve around the Sun.
examples.target_text: En nuestro sistema solar, los planetas giran en torno al Sol.

explanation_en: This expression is used to emphasize that a particular element or group of elements cannot achieve a result without external help. The pronoun 'sí' changes depending on the subject (e.g., 'por sí mismo', 'por sí solos'), which is a common grammatical hurdle for learners. It is highly versatile and used in both formal debates and everyday conversations.

examples.en_text: The children cannot solve this problem on their own; they need help.
examples.target_text: Los niños no pueden resolver este problema por sí solos; necesitan ayuda.

examples.en_text: These programs don't work by themselves, you have to configure them first.
examples.target_text: Estos programas no funcionan por sí solos, tienes que configurarlos primero.

examples.en_text: Words, on their own, cannot express everything I feel.
examples.target_text: Las palabras, por sí solas, no pueden expresar todo lo que siento.

examples.en_text: The car is not going to fix itself on its own, you have to take it to the mechanic.
examples.target_text: El coche no se va a arreglar por sí solo, tienes que llevarlo al taller.

examples.en_text: She cannot organize the whole event on her own; she needs a team.
examples.target_text: Ella no puede organizar todo el evento por sí sola; necesita un equipo.

examples.en_text: My grandparents don't want to travel on their own anymore because they get very tired.
examples.target_text: Mis abuelos ya no quieren viajar por sí solos porque se cansan mucho.

explanation_en: 'De frente' means directly, openly, or face-to-face without beating around the bush. When combined with verbs of communication like 'preguntar' or 'decir,' it implies honesty and directness, often in a confrontation. It is a very common colloquial expression across the Spanish-speaking world.

examples.en_text: I prefer that you tell me things directly instead of talking behind my back.
examples.target_text: Prefiero que me digas las cosas de frente en vez de hablar a mis espaldas.

examples.en_text: The red car collided head-on with a truck on the highway.
examples.target_text: El coche rojo chocó de frente contra un camión en la autopista.

examples.en_text: We cannot ignore this situation; we have to face the problem head-on.
examples.target_text: No podemos ignorar esta situación; hay que afrontar el problema de frente.

examples.en_text: When I asked him if it was true, he looked straight at me and told me yes.
examples.target_text: Cuando le pregunté si era verdad, me miró de frente y me dijo que sí.

examples.en_text: It was difficult to walk because the wind was blowing directly at us and it was very strong.
examples.target_text: Era difícil caminar porque el viento nos daba de frente y soplaba muy fuerte.

examples.en_text: I didn't want to beat around the bush, so I asked her point-blank if she wanted to work with us.
examples.target_text: No quería dar rodeos, así que le pregunté de frente si quería trabajar con nosotros.

explanation_en: This expression is a figurative way of saying that something affects someone deeply, emotionally, or obsessively. While it can mean to irritate (like the English 'get under my skin'), in Spanish it often carries a connotation of becoming deeply ingrained, captivating, or hard to shake off. It is a highly expressive, native-sounding phrase.

examples.en_text: That song is so beautiful that it has gotten under my skin.
examples.target_text: Esa canción es tan hermosa que se me ha metido bajo la piel.

examples.en_text: I can't stand his comments; he always finds a way to get under my skin.
examples.target_text: No soporto sus comentarios; siempre encuentra una manera de meterse bajo mi piel.

examples.en_text: Don't let her criticism get under your skin, she just wants to annoy you.
examples.target_text: No dejes que sus críticas se te metan bajo la piel, solo quiere molestarte.

examples.en_text: The story of that movie got under my skin and I couldn't stop thinking about it.
examples.target_text: La historia de esa película se me metió bajo la piel y no pude dejar de pensar en ella.

examples.en_text: His arrogant attitude got under the skin of the entire work team.
examples.target_text: Su actitud arrogante se le metió bajo la piel a todo el equipo de trabajo.

examples.en_text: I know you are trying to get under my skin, but you are not going to succeed today.
examples.target_text: Sé que estás intentando meterte bajo mi piel, pero hoy no lo vas a lograr.

explanation_en: This common fixed phrase is used to describe a situation, behavior, or phenomenon that can no longer be managed or restricted. It is equivalent to the English 'out of control' and is used in both formal news reporting and informal daily contexts. It is a vital collocation for B2/C1 learners to sound natural instead of using clunky descriptions.

examples.en_text: The forest fire is out of control due to the strong wind.
examples.target_text: El incendio forestal está fuera de control debido al fuerte viento.

examples.en_text: The situation in the office is totally out of control this week.
examples.target_text: La situación en la oficina está totalmente fuera de control esta semana.

examples.en_text: The kids are out of control today; they won't stop running around the house.
examples.target_text: Los niños están fuera de control hoy; no paran de correr por la casa.

examples.en_text: Last night's party was out of control and the neighbors called the police.
examples.target_text: La fiesta de anoche estaba fuera de control y los vecinos llamaron a la policía.

examples.en_text: I feel like my emotions are out of control lately because of stress.
examples.target_text: Siento que mis emociones están fuera de control últimamente por el estrés.

examples.en_text: Rent prices are out of control in this city.
examples.target_text: Los precios de los alquileres están fuera de control en esta ciudad.

explanation_en: The construction 'dar por + [adjective/participle]' means 'to consider or deem something to be in a certain state.' In this case, 'dar por concluido' means to officially consider something finished or closed. Note that the participle must agree in gender and number with the noun it refers to (in this case, 'las batidas').

examples.en_text: The director considered the negotiations finished after reaching an agreement.
examples.target_text: El director dio por concluidas las negociaciones después de llegar a un acuerdo.

examples.en_text: With this exam, we consider the classes for this semester finished.
examples.target_text: Con este examen, damos por concluidas las clases de este semestre.

examples.en_text: The police declared the investigations closed upon finding the culprit.
examples.target_text: La policía dio por concluidas las investigaciones al encontrar al culpable.

examples.en_text: The mayor declared the town's festivities closed with a thank-you speech.
examples.target_text: El alcalde dio por concluidas las fiestas del pueblo con un discurso de agradecimiento.

examples.en_text: We cannot consider the tasks finished until the boss reviews them.
examples.target_text: No podemos dar por concluidas las tareas hasta que el jefe las revise.

examples.en_text: After three hours of debate, the president declared today's sessions closed.
examples.target_text: Tras tres horas de debate, el presidente dio por concluidas las sesiones de hoy.

explanation_en: A highly colloquial and idiomatic Spanish expression meaning 'to get off scot-free' or 'to escape punishment or blame without consequences.' It is often used with verbs like 'irse' or 'salir.' It is perfect for C1 learners looking to sound native, especially when discussing politics, scandals, or personal accountability.

examples.en_text: The thief robbed the store and got off scot-free because the police didn't find any evidence.
examples.target_text: El ladrón robó la tienda y se fue de rositas porque la policía no encontró pruebas.

examples.en_text: It's not fair that they cheated on the exam and got away with it.
examples.target_text: No es justo que ellos copiaran en el examen y se fueran de rositas.

examples.en_text: You made a big mistake on the report, but you got off scot-free because the boss was in a good mood.
examples.target_text: Cometiste un gran error en el informe, pero te fuiste de rositas porque el jefe estaba de buen humor.

examples.en_text: We broke my mother's vase, but we got away with it because she thought it was the cat.
examples.target_text: Rompimos el jarrón de mi madre, pero nos fuimos de rositas porque pensó que había sido el gato.

examples.en_text: That corrupt politician always gets off scot-free thanks to his contacts.
examples.target_text: Ese político corrupto siempre se va de rositas gracias a sus contactos.

examples.en_text: Don't think you're going to get away with it after what you've done.
examples.target_text: No creas que te vas a ir de rositas después de lo que has hecho.

explanation_en: Literally translating to 'to shrink the heart,' this beautiful idiom is used to describe a feeling of deep sadness, grief, or empathy that makes one's heart sink. It is very common when talking about tragedies, disasters, or moving personal stories. It is used transitively, often in the form 'le encoge el corazón a alguien' or simply 'encoge el corazón' as an impersonal observation.

examples.en_text: My heart sinks every time I see a child crying in the street.
examples.target_text: Se me encoge el corazón cada vez que veo a un niño llorando en la calle.

examples.en_text: María's heart sank when she heard the news of the accident.
examples.target_text: A María se le encogió el corazón cuando escuchó la noticia del accidente.

examples.en_text: Our hearts sink every time we have to say goodbye at the airport.
examples.target_text: Se nos encoge el corazón cada vez que tenemos que despedirnos en el aeropuerto.

examples.en_text: Seeing those abandoned dogs at the shelter makes anyone's heart sink.
examples.target_text: Ver a esos perros abandonados en el refugio le encoge el corazón a cualquiera.

examples.en_text: My heart sank when I saw the empty house after the move.
examples.target_text: Se me encogió el corazón al ver la casa vacía después de la mudanza.

examples.en_text: That movie is very sad; there is a scene that really breaks your heart.
examples.target_text: Esa película es muy triste; hay una escena que realmente te encoge el corazón.

explanation_en: This common collocation means 'to downplay,' 'to play down,' or 'to minimize the importance of' something. It is constructed with the indirect object pronoun (e.g., 'le quita importancia a la situación'). It is a very natural alternative to more formal verbs like 'restar importancia' or 'minimizar.'

examples.en_text: My brother always downplays his health problems, but I am worried.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano siempre le quita importancia a sus problemas de salud, pero yo estoy preocupado.

examples.en_text: Don't downplay what happened yesterday; it was a pretty serious mistake.
examples.target_text: No le quites importancia a lo que pasó ayer; fue un error bastante grave.

examples.en_text: He tried to downplay the exam so he wouldn't get more nervous.
examples.target_text: Intentó quitarle importancia al examen para no ponerse más nervioso.

examples.en_text: The director downplayed the loss of clients during the meeting.
examples.target_text: El director le quitó importancia a la pérdida de clientes durante la reunión.

examples.en_text: It bothers me that you always downplay my feelings when we argue.
examples.target_text: Me molesta que siempre le quites importancia a mis sentimientos cuando discutimos.

examples.en_text: Although the dent on the car was bad, the mechanic has downplayed it.
examples.target_text: Aunque el golpe en el coche fue fuerte, el mecánico le ha quitado importancia.
